question: In 2026, Poland reported the jamming and spoofing of GNSS satellite navigation signals on an unprecedented scale1. Such methods of interference, which form part of Russia’s hybrid warfare against EU Member States, pose a threat to the safety of aviation and shipping, transport, telecommunications and the functioning of critical infrastructure, and may hamper military mobility on the eastern flank of the EU and NATO.

In its communication of 18 February 2026, the Commission announced plans to strengthen crisis preparedness in the eastern border regions and the resilience of critical, defence and dual-use infrastructure, including by supporting the creation of resilience clusters.

It also encouraged Member States located along the EU’s eastern border to invest in ground-based navigation infrastructure and announced support for the development of strategic border hubs for advanced regional space services through EU investment in the IRIS2 system2. In light of the above: 1.
What specific actions has the Commission taken since February 2026 to step up crisis preparedness in the eastern border regions, and how many resilience clusters have been established to date?

What measures has the Commission taken to encourage countries on the EU’s eastern border to invest in ground-based navigation systems, are such systems being developed, and have any financial resources been made available for this purpose?

What measures has the Commission taken to implement its announcement regarding the establishment of strategic hubs for advanced regional space services in the EU’s eastern border regions in conjunction with the IRIS² system, and what sources of funding and measurable targets have been set for these projects?
